This is a C++ project with a greet() function declared in src/greeter.h.

Your task:
1. Find the declaration of greet() using ast-tool:
     ast-tool find src/greeter.h greet
2. Find all call sites of greet() using ast-tool references with the line number from step 1:
     ast-tool references src/greeter.h <line>
3. In src/main.cpp, add the line
     std::cout << "Calling greet" << std::endl;
   immediately before EACH call to greet().
4. Ensure #include <iostream> is present at the top of src/main.cpp.

When done, the file src/main.cpp should compile and contain the logging statement
before every greet() call.

NAME
    find - Find AST nodes by type, text, position, or ID.

SYNOPSIS
    ast-tool find [--type <type>] [--grammar <grammar>] [--text <text>]
                  [--id <hex>] [--line <n>] [--column <n>] <file>

DESCRIPTION
    Parse <file> and print every AST node that matches all supplied
    filters simultaneously.  When no filter is given, all nodes are
    printed.

    --line and --column must be supplied together to filter by position.

ARGUMENTS
    <file>    Path to the source file to search.

OPTIONS
    --type <type>       Match nodes whose type equals <type>
                        (e.g. function_definition, identifier).
    --grammar <grammar> Match nodes whose grammar type equals <grammar>.
    --text <text>       Match nodes whose source text equals <text>.
    --id <hex>          Match the node with the given hash. Accepts
                        uppercase or lowercase hex, with or without
                        a leading 0x prefix (e.g. 9E52E360, 0x9e52e360).
    --line <n>          Match nodes that start on line <n> (1-based).
    --column <n>        Match nodes that start at column <n> (1-based).

OUTPUT
    One line per matching AST node:

        <ID> <type> @<line>:<col>[ "<text>"]

    <ID>      32-bit node hash in uppercase hexadecimal.
    <type>    Node type string.
    <line>    1-based source line.
    <col>     1-based source column.
    <text>    Source text of the node, present when non-empty.

EXAMPLES
    Find all function definitions in a file:

        ast-tool find --type function_definition src/parser.cpp

    Find the node at a specific cursor position:

        ast-tool find --line 42 --column 17 src/parser.cpp

    Find all uses of a specific identifier:

        ast-tool find --type identifier --text initialize src/main.cpp

    Look up a specific node by ID:

        ast-tool find --id <node-id> src/main.cpp

content.content:
NAME
    references - Find references to a symbol.

SYNOPSIS
    ast-tool references [--json [--pretty]] <symbol> <root>

DESCRIPTION
    Analyze the workspace rooted at <root>, resolve the named symbol, and
    print every location in the workspace where that symbol is referenced.

    Resolution is semantic, not textual: identifiers are resolved via the
    workspace symbol table, so only genuine uses of the target declaration
    are reported.  Textual grep matches are not included.

    If <symbol> contains '::' it is matched against fully-qualified names;
    otherwise it is matched against unqualified names.  If the query matches
    more than one declaration the command fails with a list of candidates;
    supply a fully-qualified name to disambiguate.

    The declaration site is excluded from results by default.

ARGUMENTS
    <symbol>  Symbol name or fully-qualified name to look up.
    <root>    Workspace root directory to scan recursively.

OPTIONS
    --json      Output results as a JSON array.
    --pretty    Pretty-print the JSON output. Implies --json.

OUTPUT
    Default (plain text), one reference per line:

        <file>:<line>:<col>

    <file>    Path of the file containing the reference.
    <line>    1-based source line of the reference.
    <col>     1-based source column of the reference.

    JSON fields per reference:

        file            Path of the file containing the reference.
        line            1-based source line of the reference.
        column          1-based source column of the reference.
        owning_scope    Lexical scope kind that encloses the reference.

    Output is sorted by file, then by line, then by column.

EXAMPLES
    Find all references to a function named 'parse':

        ast-tool references parse src/

    Find references to a fully-qualified name to disambiguate:

        ast-tool references ast::parse src/

    Export results as JSON for programmatic consumption:

        ast-tool references --json --pretty foo src/
